say: Fabric Softener and Household Cleaners. This is module 4 of the course.
We'll make a softener, a surface spray and its concentrate, a floor cleaner and a toilet descaler, and learn the mixing rules that keep people safe.

shots.label: Esterquat, about 90% active

card.title: 20 kg fabric softener
card.note: Citric acid to supplier's pH; colour from 1% stock

say: This paste on the scale is esterquat, the softening agent, often around 90% active.
It's cationic, so it clings to cotton, which carries a slight negative charge in water.
A standard softener has only about 4 to 6% active. Here's the 20 kg starting formula.

shots.label: Gloves and goggles
say: Esterquat can irritate eyes and skin, and you'll handle it warm. Gloves and goggles on, and move carefully to avoid burns.

shots.label: Esterquat into warm water
say: Heat the water to the temperature on your supplier's sheet, and acidify it slightly if the sheet says so.
Watch: the softened esterquat pours slowly into the warm water while we stir steadily, and it turns milky white.
Keep stirring as it cools and thickens. Below about 40 degrees, add fragrance, preservative and colour.

shots.banner: Softener in the final rinse only
say: Blessing in Benin City worked this out at her desk. About 33 rinses a bottle, roughly ₦45 a wash at her approximate price.
Tell every customer: wash and rinse with detergent first. Softener goes only in the final rinse, never mixed with detergent.

shots.label: Multipurpose surface spray
say: See how the spray mists the counter and wipes off without streaks. Low foam, low residue, quick drying.
A nonionic surfactant cleans with little foam, and isopropyl alcohol lifts grease and speeds drying.
Mix the fragrance into the surfactant until clear before it goes into the water.

shots.label: Open window, no flames
say: Mix this spray by an open window like this one, away from flames, cooking gas and generators. Keep the drum closed.
And never add bleach, quats or acids to make it stronger. That creates dangerous mixtures.

shots.label: Concentrate to ready-to-use
say: Offices like a concentrate. Look along these cups from strong to weak.
1:19 means 1 part concentrate plus 19 parts water. Aisha in Abuja gives her office a 25 ml measuring cup and a printed dilution card.

shots.label: Test on a hidden spot
say: Always test your own dilution before delivery, on a greasy desk and a glass panel. Then try a small hidden spot, let it dry, and check for dulling.

shots.label: Floor cleaner in a 5-litre bucket
say: Now the floor cleaner concentrate pours into a bucket of water. It should mix in quickly with no oily drops floating, and little foam.
Funmi in Akure found 40 ml per bucket cleaned well without leaving the floor sticky, and gave a school a clear monthly order figure.

shots.label: Citric acid
say: Scale in the toilet bowl needs an acid. We use citric acid, not hydrochloric acid, which gives off corrosive fumes and causes severe burns.
Disperse the xanthan gum slowly into stirring water first, then dissolve the citric acid. The thickening helps the gel cling under the rim.

shots.label: Descaler: strongly acidic
say: Test the finished descaler with a strip. It should read strongly acidic. Pack it with a child-resistant cap.

shots.label: Bleach and acid cleaner
shots.banner: Never mix bleach with acid or ammonia
say: Look at these two bottles, kept apart. Bleach plus an acid toilet cleaner or vinegar releases chlorine gas, which damages the lungs.
Bleach plus ammonia cleaners releases chloramine gases. Use one product, rinse or flush, then the next.

shots.label: Fresh air first
say: If someone breathes fumes from mixed cleaners, get them into fresh air at once and seek medical help. Open the windows, and don't go back into the closed bathroom.

shots.label: If in eyes: plenty of water
say: Print first aid on the descaler label: if in eyes, rinse with plenty of water and get medical advice.
If swallowed, rinse the mouth, do not induce vomiting, and get medical help immediately.
Now go through the lessons below. Make your softener test batch, try your spray and concentrate, and write your dose card and warning label. Then teach the never-mix rules to someone at home.
